update the device card — the device card is the durable cross-session
record. (Cell 1's `GATES["..."]["limit"]` isn't the right surface; kernel
resets are typically a new notebook anyway.)

### HERA handshake

When HERA is proposing the cells: it provides Cell A and Cell B together
but **does not propose any subsequent recipe step until the human reports
the discovered ranges and the validator cell has been run**. Asking for
the limits is the explicit handshake. Human is the gate; HERA waits.

### Failure-mode catalog

| What you see on the live plot | What it means | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Lock-in `X` nonzero and smoothly varying | Device alive, contact wiring good | Continue |
| Lock-in `X` flat zero on one channel | Wiring break on that contact pair | Stop; check wiring |

| `k_bg.curr` (parked gate) tracks the `k_tg` sweep | Cross-gate leakage path | Stop; characterize via `gate-leakage-survey` |

## Examples

  iterate-then-bless framing: three small fixed `0 → +1 V` sweeps (TG, BG,

  to ground potential). After ungrounding, manual range-finding established

zero field, via `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, ..., k_bg.volt, ...)`. All lock-in
channels read at every grid point; gate-current channels monitored for live
leakage. The first map you take when cap ratios `dtg` / `dbg` are not yet
trusted — sweeping in raw gate voltages avoids any `(n, D) ↔ (V_tg, V_bg)`
calibration error. Plots via
`sharpelab_nb.plotting.plot_gatemap(file_path, file, nD=True)` (the analysis
side reprojects to physical `(n, D)` after the fact, using the cap ratios
in scope at plot time — separate from the sweep itself).

For the polygon-in-`(n, D)` variant (rasterized parallelogram via
`raster.rasterize` + `multisweep`), see `nD-map`. The two recipes share
external structure (AsyncStation, fp/plot, comments) but differ in their
sweep call and their cap-ratio dependency.

## When

`gate-current-sanity-check` with Cell B committed (the safe `(V_tg, V_bg)`
ranges define the maximum extent of the megasweep box) and, for
rhombohedral devices, `silicon-backgate-survey` (`V_si` is held at the
operating point this gatemap commits to). A `gate-leakage-survey` should
have been done already — or, for any gatemap that ventures far from
`(0, 0)`, have a leakage-check `register_run_before` callback installed
(see `gate-leakage-survey` Flavor B). After the first gatemap is in hand,
the campaign branches by scientific question (see `## Next`).

The natural predecessor of `nD-map`: a clean axis-aligned gatemap is the
substrate from which `cap-ratio-calibration` extracts the CNP slope, which
is what makes a polygon-in-`(n, D)` sweep trustworthy.

## Why
The gatemap is the only measurement in the toploader pipeline that surveys
the gate plane densely without committing to a particular feature or to a
particular set of cap ratios. Every downstream Block 1 recipe targets a
specific point or line — and you can only pick one if you've seen the
map. A 201×201 megasweep at `slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1` takes ~3.5 hours
and is the densest first-look you can get without dropping into
rasterized-polygon sweeps (`nD-map`).

The axis-aligned form has two failure modes the polygon form doesn't:
(1) it wastes 30–60% of points outside the safe polygon when the
`(n, D)` region of interest is a tilted parallelogram, and (2) on a
device with strongly-coupled top/bottom gates, a rectangle in
`(V_tg, V_bg)` is a sheared parallelogram in `(n, D)` and the CNP cuts
the rectangle diagonally. Both are worth tolerating on the *first* map,
because the alternative requires cap ratios you don't yet trust.

## Recipe

1. Decide the `(V_bg, V_tg)` extent. Stay strictly inside the validators
   set by the device-init recipes; for a first gatemap pick a rectangle
   that brackets the working setpoint with margin (e.g.
   `V_bg ∈ [-8, 6.5]`, `V_tg ∈ [-6.5, 6.5]` for a 25.5/16 nm device at
   `V_si = 48 V`).
2. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('gatemap')` first,
   then optional structured tags identifying the operating point, e.g.
   `s.add_comment(f'MC{N}, Vsi = {V_si}V')`. Call
   `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` if the notebook has the helper (RPL_19

   `k_bg.curr` and `'time'` vs `k_tg.curr` / `k_si.curr` so live leakage
   is visible; for a survey gatemap also `s.plot(k_bg.volt, sr.X)` over

5. (Optional) `s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s, [sr830s_2_autorange])`

   leaves this commented out for the canonical 201×201 — autorange

```python
from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run
import numpy as np

run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
print(summarize_run(run))

#         tags carrying MC label / Vsi.

#    operator stop; treat as block until the human explains.

# 2. Leakage stayed below threshold across the whole map. Threshold matches
#    the gate-leakage-survey abort thresholds (~5e-11 to 8e-11 A); use 1 nA

        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} is flat across the map — check lock-in / wiring")
    if np.isnan(x).any():

# 4. Eyeball the rendered plot — Read('<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>/plot.png').

#    transitions) are easier to assess visually than numerically; the
```

# (3) channels independent (no grounded-device short), (4) BG/Si leakage at floor.
# NOT range-finding (blocklisted): TG stays well inside the provided [-6,+7] V
# validator (sweep -3..+3 V). Current-bias (5 nA) -> modulation is in the Rxx
# voltage channels; sr0 (drain current) should stay ~constant.

# --- preconditions (state this cell assumes but does not set) ---

assert abs(B0) < 0.01, f'field not ~0: {B0} T'
assert T0 < 1.5,       f'T not at base: {T0} K'
assert abs(k_bg.volt()) < 1e-6 and abs(k_2410.volt()) < 1e-6, 'BG/Si not parked at 0'
print(f'preconditions OK: B={B0:.4f} T, T={T0:.3f} K, BG={k_bg.volt()} V, Si={k_2410.volt()} V')

# --- route the provided contacts (Si 16/11 standing closures are unmanaged/untouched) ---
mux.select({"source": "T2", "drain": "B7",
            "sr1+": "T3", "sr1-": "T4",
            "sr2+": "B4", "sr2-": "B5",
            "sr3+": "T5", "sr3-": "B6"})
print('routed:', mux.mc_fragment())

# --- lock-in sensitivity: 5 mV headroom on the Rxx/Rxy channels so a CNP peak
#     (R up to ~1 MOhm at 5 nA bias) does not overload. Config choice, reversible.
for s_ in (sr1, sr2, sr3):
    s_.sensitivity(0.005)

# --- per-run measurement config (structured, current; no inherited text) ---
meas_config["sr0"] = "drain current on B7 (Ithaco x-1e6)"
meas_config["sr1"] = "Rxx T3-T4"
meas_config["sr2"] = "Rxx B4-B5"
meas_config["sr3"] = "Rxy T5-B6"
meas_config["bias_voltage"] = sr1.amplitude()
meas_config["lockin_freq"] = sr1.frequency()
meas_config["sr0_sens"] = sr0.sensitivity()
meas_config["sr1_sens"] = sr1.sensitivity()
meas_config["sr2_sens"] = sr2.sensitivity()
meas_config["sr3_sens"] = sr3.sensitivity()
meas_config["sample_temperature:"] = heater.sample_temperature()
meas_config["Si (V)"] = k_2410.volt()
meas_config["comments"] = ("Gate C liveness: TG -3..+3 V, BG=Si=0, B=0, "
                           "provided config src T2/drain B7; sr1/2/3 sens 5 mV")

# --- build station fresh (comments are station-lifetime; rebuild per intent) ---
s = async_station(meas_config)
s.add_comment('gate-current-sanity-check')
s.add_comment('Gate C liveness - provided contact config; TG trace BG=Si=0 B=0')

s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0.0)   # BG already 0; never s.ramp(dc205_volt) -> it has no get

s.fp(heater.sample_temperature)
s.fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(k_2410.curr)
for lia in (sr0, sr1, sr2, sr3):
    s.fp(lia.X).fp(lia.P)

s.plot(dc205_volt, sr1.X)
s.plot(dc205_volt, sr2.X)
s.plot(dc205_volt, sr0.X)

# TG sweep -3 -> +3 V (well inside validator), 61 pts, 2.0 s dwell (~settling floor)
try:
    s.sweep(dc205_volt, spoints(-3.0, 3.0, 61), delay=2.0)
finally:
    dc205_volt(0.0)   # park TG via direct set (s.ramp would call the missing get)
print('Gate C liveness sweep done; TG parked at 0.')

# === Gate C — cheap liveness on the provided contacts (v2, LS335 fix) ===
# Re-run of cell 30 (errored: per-point heater.sample_temperature poll hit the
# LS335/Grafana VISA-contention quirk). Fix: NO Lakeshore poll inside the loop.
# T is snapshotted once in meas_config; the Grafana logger keeps the time series.
# Otherwise identical: provided contacts, TG -3..+3 V trace, BG=Si=0, B=0.
# Current-bias (5 nA) -> modulation lives in Rxx (sr1/sr2); sr0 (I) ~constant.

# --- preconditions (state this cell assumes but does not set) ---
B0 = magnet.mag(); T0 = heater.sample_temperature()   # single reads OK; not per-point
assert abs(B0) < 0.01, f'field not ~0: {B0} T'
assert T0 < 1.5,       f'T not at base: {T0} K'
assert abs(k_bg.volt()) < 1e-6 and abs(k_2410.volt()) < 1e-6, 'BG/Si not parked at 0'
print(f'preconditions OK: B={B0:.4f} T, T={T0:.3f} K, TG(k_tg)={k_tg.voltage()} V, '
      f'BG={k_bg.volt()} V, Si={k_2410.volt()} V')

# --- route the provided contacts (Si 16/11 standing closures unmanaged/untouched) ---
mux.select({"source": "T2", "drain": "B7",
            "sr1+": "T3", "sr1-": "T4",
            "sr2+": "B4", "sr2-": "B5",
            "sr3+": "T5", "sr3-": "B6"})
print('routed:', mux.mc_fragment())

# --- 5 mV headroom on Rxx/Rxy channels so a CNP peak does not overload ---
for s_ in (sr1, sr2, sr3):
    s_.sensitivity(0.005)

# --- per-run measurement config ---
meas_config["sr0"] = "drain current on B7 (Ithaco x-1e6)"
meas_config["sr1"] = "Rxx T3-T4"
meas_config["sr2"] = "Rxx B4-B5"
meas_config["sr3"] = "Rxy T5-B6"
meas_config["bias_voltage"] = sr1.amplitude()
meas_config["lockin_freq"] = sr1.frequency()
meas_config["sr0_sens"] = sr0.sensitivity()
meas_config["sr1_sens"] = sr1.sensitivity()
meas_config["sr2_sens"] = sr2.sensitivity()
meas_config["sr3_sens"] = sr3.sensitivity()
meas_config["sample_temperature:"] = heater.sample_temperature()
meas_config["Si (V)"] = k_2410.volt()
meas_config["comments"] = ("Gate C liveness v2 (LS335 fix): TG -3..+3 V, BG=Si=0, B=0, "
                           "provided config src T2/drain B7; sr1/2/3 sens 5 mV")

# --- build station fresh ---
s = async_station(meas_config)
s.add_comment('gate-current-sanity-check')
s.add_comment('Gate C liveness v2 - no LS335 per-point poll')

s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0.0)   # BG already 0; never s.ramp(dc205_volt) -> no get

# Followed params: NO heater.sample_temperature (LS335 contention).
s.fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(k_2410.curr)
for lia in (sr0, sr1, sr2, sr3):
    s.fp(lia.X).fp(lia.P)

s.plot(dc205_volt, sr1.X)
s.plot(dc205_volt, sr2.X)
s.plot(dc205_volt, sr0.X)

try:
    s.sweep(dc205_volt, spoints(-3.0, 3.0, 61), delay=2.0)
finally:
    dc205_volt(0.0)   # park TG via direct set
print('Gate C liveness v2 done; TG parked at 0.')

1	# SdH spot check
2	
3	## What
4	A fixed-(n, D) magnetic-field sweep **from zero**, designed to resolve
5	Shubnikov–de Haas / quantum-oscillation **frequency content** at one density — the
6	onset field and the tone frequencies — by FFT in 1/B. Mechanically this is a
7	`field-sweep-1d` (see it for the Station / sweep / fp / plot call surface); what
8	makes it a *spot check* is the design discipline below — the field range, B-step,
9	and settling are chosen to resolve the tones cleanly, and the read is the 1/B FFT.
10	It is the cheap 1D precursor to a `landau-fan`: one density, but **full per-point
11	quality**.
12	
13	## When
14	- **Before committing a `landau-fan`.** A spot check pins the **onset** (sets the
15	  fan's B-range), the **observed tone frequencies** (confirm/correct the fan's
16	  B-step), and the **settling/sensitivity** the fan inherits. A fan is the dense
17	  version; a couple of clean spot checks de-risk it — and can answer the question
18	  outright (`investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md` Step 3).
19	- Whenever a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap` showed QO-like wiggles and you want the
20	  frequency content at a point, not the whole (n, B) plane.
21	
22	## Why
23	A spot check is cheap because it is **one density (1D), not because it is
24	low-quality**. Its whole value is being acquired *well* — at the settling floor and
25	Nyquist on the fastest tone — so a clean spot check can be decisive on its own and a
26	noisier fan cannot overturn it (`landau-fan`). Two knobs carry the quality:
27	
28	- **Sampling.** The fastest tone sets the finest 1/B period. The reference frequency
29	  **F_L = (h/g·e)·n** (g = 4) — what a single four-fold pocket carrying all the
30	  density would give — is an upper bound on the fastest tone; Nyquist it. Undersampling
31	  the fast tone folds its aliases into the low-frequency band, where they masquerade
32	  as a small/slow tone (Verify).
33	- **Settling.** A swept-point dwell has a floor near the lock-in time constant
34	  (dwell ≥ k·τ; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct). Under-settling **attenuates
35	  the oscillation amplitude itself** (the filter cannot track the QO) — benign on a
36	  smooth slope, but it *buries a small tone* (Verify). The floor is non-negotiable
37	  when the target is a weak tone.
38	
39	## Recipe
40	1. **Density + range.** Pick the density — high |n| gives the most periods and the
41	   clearest tones. Sweep B **from 0** to a target field: starting at zero captures the
42	   **onset** (the lowest B where oscillations appear once the MR background is
43	   subtracted). Use a **uniform B-step** (non-uniform steps complicate the 1/B FFT).
44	2. **B-step from F_L.** Compute F_L = (h/4e)·n and set ΔB to Nyquist-resolve it —
45	   ≥ 2 (prefer 3) samples per the fastest 1/B period, evaluated at the high-field end
46	   where the period is finest. This is the B-step a committed fan inherits.
47	3. **Lock-in.** Set sensitivity so full scale ≈ I_bias × R_target — a signal at a
48	   few % of range is coarse-ADC digitized (the grainy-FFT failure). Set the dwell at
49	   the settling floor (Why); read τ and the filter slope, do not guess them.
50	4. **The sweep.** Run it as a `field-sweep-1d` (its Recipe is the call surface):
51	   build the Station, ramp the gates to (n, D), `s.sweep(mag.field, field_vec,
52	   delay=dwell)` with a uniform `field_vec` from 0, fp the temperature(s) and every
53	   lock-in X/P, plot the live MR and gate-current leakage.
54	5. **FFT read.** Re-form Rxx from the TSV (rendered PNGs alias). Subtract the
55	   monotonic MR background — a **5th-order polynomial** is usually fine, provided the
56	   field range is wide enough that the polynomial captures the background without
57	   absorbing the oscillations — to get ΔRxx(B). Read the **onset** off ΔRxx — the low-field point
58	   where oscillations emerge — and use it as the **low-field cutoff of the FFT window**
59	   (field below onset adds background, no signal). Over [onset, B_max]: resample ΔRxx to
60	   even 1/B, window, FFT. Read the **tone frequencies** against F_L, and — for
61	   FS-counting — the peak set per the combinatorics in
62	   `investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md`.
63	
64	## Verify
65	- **Settling — under-settling buries a small tone.** A dwell below the floor
66	  attenuates the oscillation amplitude (the filter can't track it). On a smooth slope
67	  that's a benign uniform lag; when the target is a small/weak tone it *erases* the
68	  feature. Non-negotiable for a weak-tone hunt; bend it only for a slope read on a
69	  strong signal.
70	- **Sampling — an undersampled fast tone aliases down.** If ΔB under-samples the
71	  fastest tone (≈ F_L), its aliases fold into the low-frequency band and masquerade
72	  as a small/slow tone. Nyquist the *fast* tone even when the target is the slow one
73	  (worked case: Examples).
74	- **FFT stability sweep.** Vary the detrender (high-pass scale) and the window; a real
75	  peak **sharpens** as the 1/B record lengthens, an alias/artifact **wanders**.
76	- **Onset is read from the background-subtracted data, not the FFT.** It is the
77	  low-field point where oscillations emerge in ΔRxx(B) (the MR background removed) —
78	  the **low-field cutoff for the FFT window**, not a quantity the FFT returns. Report
79	  it: it sets a fan's B-range and tracks quantum mobility (an onset that rises on a
80	  later cooldown is a device-quality regression).
81	
82	## Examples
83	- *(our-measurement, QC0426/VTI 2026-06-16)* — at n = +8×10¹² a **12.5 mT** spot check
84	  resolved two tones (a main tone + a low-frequency partner) summing to F_L, where a
85	  same-session fan run at a coarser B-step and under-settled did not. A prior **50 mT**
86	  step had under-sampled the ~83 T main tone, folding its aliases into the small-tone
87	  band. The worked case for "acquire the spot check well, *then* commit the fan."
88	
89	## Next
90	- **Clean QO, tones resolved** → run a `landau-fan`, inheriting this spot check's
91	  B-step, settling, and onset; or take a couple more spot checks across density for a
92	  cheap preview of the n-dependence.
93	- **Two tones at D ≈ 0** → `investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md` (the
94	  FS-count combinatorics).
95	- **Tone amplitude vs T wanted** (effective mass) → `temperature-dependence`
96	  Flavor B.

and settling are chosen to resolve the tones cleanly, and the read is the 1/B FFT.
It is the cheap 1D precursor to a `landau-fan`: one density, but **full per-point
quality**.

  outright (`investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md` Step 3).

  frequency content at a point, not the whole (n, B) plane.

low-quality**. Its whole value is being acquired *well* — at the settling floor and

  as a small/slow tone (Verify).
- **Settling.** A swept-point dwell has a floor near the lock-in time constant
  (dwell ≥ k·τ; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct). Under-settling **attenuates
  the oscillation amplitude itself** (the filter cannot track the QO) — benign on a
  smooth slope, but it *buries a small tone* (Verify). The floor is non-negotiable
  when the target is a weak tone.

   field range is wide enough that the polynomial captures the background without
   absorbing the oscillations — to get ΔRxx(B). Read the **onset** off ΔRxx — the low-field point
   where oscillations emerge — and use it as the **low-field cutoff of the FFT window**

   even 1/B, window, FFT. Read the **tone frequencies** against F_L, and — for
   FS-counting — the peak set per the combinatorics in
   `investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md`.

- **Settling — under-settling buries a small tone.** A dwell below the floor

  that's a benign uniform lag; when the target is a small/weak tone it *erases* the

  strong signal.

  fastest tone (≈ F_L), its aliases fold into the low-frequency band and masquerade
  as a small/slow tone. Nyquist the *fast* tone even when the target is the slow one
  (worked case: Examples).

  the **low-field cutoff for the FFT window**, not a quantity the FFT returns. Report
  it: it sets a fan's B-range and tracks quantum mobility (an onset that rises on a
  later cooldown is a device-quality regression).

## Examples

  resolved two tones (a main tone + a low-frequency partner) summing to F_L, where a

  step had under-sampled the ~83 T main tone, folding its aliases into the small-tone
  band. The worked case for "acquire the spot check well, *then* commit the fan."

# Trilayer FS-count forward model — ABA vs ABC

Backs the `recipes/investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md` investigation.
Where `models/aba_trilayer/` computes the **Landau-fan crossing structure** (the
Datta fingerprint), this model computes the **B = 0 Fermi-surface count** and the
**Onsager frequencies** the FS-count read overlays on data: ABA ≥ 2 coexisting
surfaces (ML Dirac + BL parabolic) vs ABC's single post-Lifshitz pocket.

The survey that grounds it (band structure, the three ingested papers, the
feasibility numbers) is `docs/stacking-extraction-survey.md`; read it for the
physics. This README covers what the tools are and how to run them.

## Files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `fs_count_b0.py` | B = 0 FS count + Onsager F(n, D). **ABA** from the continuum 6-site SWMcC Hamiltonian (Datta params, γ₃=γ₄=0 — same parameters as `models/aba_trilayer/ll_spectrum.py`); **ABC** from the MacDonald PRB 82, 035409 (2010) effective two-band model (Eq. 6/7) with trigonal warping → the 3-pocket → annulus → single-pocket Lifshitz cascade. Counts distinct extremal-orbit frequencies F = (ℏ/2πe)·A_k. Pure numpy/scipy. |
| `plots.py` | Renders `{aba_bands_linecut, abc_bands_linecut, abc_bands_contour, luttinger_vs_n}.png` from `fs_count_b0`. |
| `ll_sequence.py` | High-field complement: ABA Landau-level fan + QH/Streda sequence (the pseudo-decoupled ML Dirac band offsets the Chern sequence; non-dispersing ML N=0 doublet). Imports the validated `models/aba_trilayer/ll_spectrum.py`. Outputs `aba_LL_fan.png`, `aba_wannier.png`. |
| `*.png` | Generated figures (band linecuts, ABC contour, Luttinger-sum check, LL fan, Wannier diagram). |
| `rmg-fft-snapshot/` | Frozen copy of the RMG SdH-FFT analysis pipeline (background-subtract in B → interp to 1/B → window → FFT, with the stability-sweep hygiene). A **reference snapshot, not a standalone package** — see its `PROVENANCE.md`; reconcile into `hera.analysis.sdh_fft` later. |

## Run

```bash
cd hera/models/trilayer_fs_count
uv run --no-project --with numpy --with scipy python3 fs_count_b0.py              # FS count + Onsager frequencies
uv run --no-project --with numpy --with scipy --with matplotlib python3 plots.py # band/Luttinger figures
uv run --no-project --with numpy --with scipy --with matplotlib python3 ll_sequence.py  # high-field Streda fan
```
(`--no-project` pulls just numpy/scipy/matplotlib — the worktree's submodules
aren't checked out, so `uv sync` can't run here.)

## Validation

- **Luttinger sum** Σf = n at the right degeneracy reproduces in both models at
  every density tested — the model-independent consistency check on the count.
- `fs_count_b0` reproduces MacDonald's trigonal-warping Lifshitz cascade location
  (~10¹¹ cm⁻²), so ABC presents a single Fermi surface at the ~10¹² operating
  density.
- `ll_sequence` builds on the already-validated `aba_trilayer/ll_spectrum.py`
  (the 2 meV / 14 meV band splittings gate that model).

## Gap / future work

A quantitative **ABC** Landau-level model is **not yet built** — only ABA is
computed, so the high-field Streda/Chern contrast (recipe Step 6) is qualitative
on the ABC side. See `docs/stacking-extraction-survey.md` §9. A candidate
implementation to adapt is Dan Parker's `RhombohedralGrapheneLandau.jl`, though
it appears R4G (tetralayer)-specific and would need trilayer adaptation.

**Onsager F(n) is numerically clamped above |n| ≈ 3.5e12 cm⁻²** (`aba_fs` E_F
search capped at 70 meV; `abc_fs` a 50 meV window + `kmax`): above the density
the energy/k grid reaches, `np.interp` clamps to the grid edge instead of
failing, so F(n) **flattens spuriously**. This is a solver-domain artifact, *not*
a model-validity limit. Consequence: the curves do not reach the QC0426 operating
density (±8e12), so the Step-5 overlay cannot currently be run at the operating
point. **TODO (Aaron + Claude to revisit):** extend the grids to cover the
operating range, and/or make the solver raise/NaN above its covered range rather
than silently clamp.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run

r = open_run('data/1')
mc = r.metadata['measurement_config']
Ibias = mc['bias_voltage'] / mc['bias_resistor']
g0 = mc['sr0_gain']

V   = r.col('DC_bias')
I   = r.col('sr0_X') / g0                 # drain current (A)
Rxx1 = r.col('sr1_X') / Ibias             # Rxx T3-T4 (Ohm)
Rxx2 = r.col('sr2_X') / Ibias             # Rxx B4-B5
Rxy3 = r.col('sr3_X') / Ibias             # Rxy T5-B6
ibg = r.col('k_bg_curr'); isi = r.col('k_2410_curr')

print(f'I_bias = {Ibias*1e9:.3f} nA ; sr0_gain={g0:g}')
print(f'sr0 drain I: med {np.median(I)*1e9:.3f} nA, min {I.min()*1e9:.3f}, max {I.max()*1e9:.3f}  (flat => current-bias OK)')
print(f'sr1 Rxx: min {np.nanmin(Rxx1):.1f}  max {np.nanmax(Rxx1):.1f}  @Vpeak={V[np.nanargmax(Rxx1)]:.3f} V')
print(f'sr2 Rxx: min {np.nanmin(Rxx2):.1f}  max {np.nanmax(Rxx2):.1f}  @Vpeak={V[np.nanargmax(Rxx2)]:.3f} V')
print(f'sr3 Rxy: min {np.nanmin(Rxy3):.1f}  max {np.nanmax(Rxy3):.1f}')
print(f'LEAKAGE k_bg.curr:  max|I| {np.abs(ibg).max():.3e} A')
print(f'LEAKAGE k_2410.curr: max|I| {np.abs(isi).max():.3e} A')
# channel-independence / grounded-short check
print(f'corr(sr1,sr2) = {np.corrcoef(Rxx1,Rxx2)[0,1]:.3f} ; identical? {np.allclose(Rxx1,Rxx2)}')
# quantization step
dq = np.diff(np.unique(np.round(Rxx1,3)))
print(f'sr1 R smallest level step ~ {np.min(dq[dq>0]):.2f} Ohm (digitization grain)')

fig, ax = plt.subplots(2,1, figsize=(7,7), sharex=True)
ax[0].plot(V, Rxx1, '.-', label='sr1 Rxx T3-T4')
ax[0].plot(V, Rxx2, '.-', label='sr2 Rxx B4-B5')
ax[0].set_ylabel('Rxx (Ohm)'); ax[0].legend(); ax[0].grid(alpha=.3)
ax[0].set_title('Gate C liveness (run 1): TG trace, BG=Si=0, B=0  [sens 5mV -> quantized]')
ax[1].plot(V, I*1e9, '.-', color='k', label='sr0 drain I (nA)')
ax[1].plot(V, Rxy3, '.-', color='C3', label='sr3 Rxy (Ohm)')
ax[1].set_xlabel('DC_bias = V_TG (V)'); ax[1].legend(); ax[1].grid(alpha=.3)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('hera_scratch/ana_gateC.png', dpi=110)
print('saved hera_scratch/ana_gateC.png')

```python
import os
import json

import numpy as np
import scipy.constants as cst
import matplotlib as mpl
import matplotlib.colors as mcolors
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from sweep import sweep_load as sl
from pathlib import Path

%matplotlib inline

cst_e = cst.e
cst_h = cst.h
Rq = cst_h/cst_e**2

def _resolve_data_dir():
    """Locate this run's ./data dir from the notebook's own location.

    The ana kernel's cwd is not guaranteed to be the measurement dir, so a
    bare './data' breaks loaders with FileNotFoundError. IPython sets
    globals()['_dh'] to a list whose first entry is the notebook's startup
    cwd (the dir holding the notebook); this survives jupyter-collaboration/
    RTC and any later %cd, so we prefer it. We fall back to Path.cwd() and
    search a few levels up so loading still works if the kernel started inside
    ./data/<id>/. The walk stops before the filesystem root so an unrelated
    top-level 'data' dir can never be matched.
    """
    candidates = []
    dh = globals().get("_dh")
    if dh:
        candidates.append(Path(dh[0]))
    candidates.append(Path.cwd())
    for base in candidates:
        base = Path(base).resolve()
        for d in [base, *base.parents]:
            if d == d.parent:  # filesystem root
                break
            cand = d / "data"
            if cand.is_dir():
                return str(cand)
    return str((Path(candidates[0]) / "data").resolve())


file_path = _resolve_data_dir()


def load1d(i):
    return np.loadtxt(os.path.join(file_path, "{:d}".format(i), "data.tsv.gz"))

def load_meta(i):
    fp = open(os.path.join(file_path, "{:d}".format(i), "metadata.json"), "r")
    return json.load(fp)

def pretty_load(i):
    data = load1d(i)
    meta = load_meta(i)

    data_dict = {}
    for ind, col in enumerate(meta['columns']):
        data_dict[col] = data[:, ind]

    return data_dict

def pretty_load2d(i):
    data = np.loadtxt(os.path.join(file_path, "{:d}".format(i), "data.tsv"))
    meta = load_meta(i)

    data_dict = {}
    for ind, col in enumerate(meta['columns']):
        data_dict[col] = data[:, ind]

    return data_dict
```

```python
cst_epsilon0 = cst.epsilon_0
cst_e = cst.e
cst_h = cst.h
cst_phi0 = cst_h/(2*cst_e)
cst_kappa_SiO2 = 3.9

def calc_ctg(t_tg):
    """
    Calculates area capacitance for a top gate
    """
    return cst_epsilon0*cst_kappa_hBN/t_tg

def calc_cbg(t_bg, t_bgSiO2):
    """

    """
```

# Gate C liveness (run 1) — provided contact config, TG trace at BG=Si=0, B=0.
# RAW first: drain current + per-channel Rxx/Rxy vs TG. Current-bias => modulation
# is in the Rxx voltage channels; sr0 (drain current) is forced ~constant.
d = pretty_load(1)
m = load_meta(1)
mc = m['measurement_config']
Ibias = mc['bias_voltage'] / mc['bias_resistor']      # 5 nA
g0 = mc['sr0_gain']                                    # -1e6

V    = d['DC_bias']
I    = d['sr0_X'] / g0
Rxx1 = d['sr1_X'] / Ibias                              # T3-T4
Rxx2 = d['sr2_X'] / Ibias                              # B4-B5
Rxy3 = d['sr3_X'] / Ibias                              # T5-B6 (Hall cross; B=0)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(7, 7), sharex=True)
ax[0].plot(V, Rxx1, '.-', label='sr1 Rxx T3-T4')
ax[0].plot(V, Rxx2, '.-', label='sr2 Rxx B4-B5')
ax[0].set_ylabel(r'$R_{xx}$ ($\Omega$)'); ax[0].legend(); ax[0].grid(alpha=.3)
ax[0].set_title('Gate C liveness (run 1): TG trace, BG=Si=0, B=0')
ax[1].plot(V, I*1e9, '.-k', label='sr0 drain I (nA)')
ax[1].plot(V, Rxy3, '.-', color='C3', label=r'sr3 $R_{xy}$ ($\Omega$, B=0)')
ax[1].set_xlabel('$V_{TG}$ (DC_bias, V)'); ax[1].legend(); ax[1].grid(alpha=.3)
plt.show()

print(f'I_bias = {Ibias*1e9:.2f} nA | drain I: med {np.median(I)*1e9:.2f} nA '
      f'(flat across sweep -> current-bias OK, current passes)')
print(f'Rxx peak: sr1 {np.nanmax(Rxx1):.0f} ohm @ V_TG={V[np.nanargmax(Rxx1)]:.2f} ; '
      f'sr2 {np.nanmax(Rxx2):.0f} ohm @ V_TG={V[np.nanargmax(Rxx2)]:.2f}')
print(f'channel independence: corr(sr1,sr2)={np.corrcoef(Rxx1,Rxx2)[0,1]:.3f}, '
      f'identical={np.allclose(Rxx1,Rxx2)} (not identical -> no grounded short)')
print(f'leakage: |I_bg|max={np.abs(d["k_bg_curr"]).max():.2e} A, '
      f'|I_si|max={np.abs(d["k_2410_curr"]).max():.2e} A (both at/near floor)')
print('VERDICT: device alive, passes current, gate-responsive (CNP near V_TG~0 at '
      'BG=0), channels independent, leakage at floor. Gate C PASS. '
      'Note: low device R (~kohm) -> data here quantized at 5 mV sens; '
      'CNP shows a double-peak common to both Rxx channels (real feature, not a '
      'per-contact mosaic offset) to resolve in the 2D map.')

import numpy as np, json
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
import scipy.constants as cst

m = json.load(open('data/2/metadata.json')); cols = m['columns']
raw = np.loadtxt('data/2/data.tsv.gz')
ci = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(cols)}
mc = m['measurement_config']
Ibias = mc['bias_voltage'] / mc['bias_resistor']

BGv = np.unique(raw[:, ci['k_bg_volt']])     # slow, 25
TGv = np.unique(raw[:, ci['DC_bias']])        # fast, 61
nBG, nTG = len(BGv), len(TGv)
print(f'grid: {nBG} BG x {nTG} TG ; Ibias={Ibias*1e9:.2f} nA ; npts={len(raw)}')

def grid(col):
    g = (raw[:, ci[col]] / Ibias).reshape(nBG, nTG)
    return g
R1 = grid('sr1_X'); R2 = grid('sr2_X'); R3 = grid('sr3_X')
# BG ascending in setpoints (-4.5..+4.5); TG ascending (-6..+6) within each row.
# raw row order: slow ascending, fast ascending -> reshape(nBG,nTG) rows=BG.

# --- CNP ridge per channel: argmax over TG per BG row, smoothed; edge guard ---
def ridge(R):
    tg_cnp = np.full(nBG, np.nan); rmax = np.full(nBG, np.nan); edge = np.zeros(nBG, bool)
    for i in range(nBG):
        prof = gaussian_filter1d(R[i], 1.5)
        j = int(np.nanargmax(prof))
        tg_cnp[i] = TGv[j]; rmax[i] = R[i][j]
        if j <= 1 or j >= nTG - 2:
            edge[i] = True
    return tg_cnp, rmax, edge

for name, R in [('sr1 T3-T4', R1), ('sr2 B4-B5', R2)]:
    tg_cnp, rmax, edge = ridge(R)
    good = ~edge & np.isfinite(tg_cnp)
    p = np.polyfit(BGv[good], tg_cnp[good], 1)
    resid = tg_cnp[good] - np.polyval(p, BGv[good])
    slope, intc = p
    c_bg_over_c_tg = -slope
    print(f'\n[{name}]  rows used {good.sum()}/{nBG} (edge-excluded {edge.sum()})')
    print(f'  CNP line: V_tg = {slope:+.4f}*V_bg + {intc:+.4f}')
    print(f'  ratio c_bg/c_tg = -slope = {c_bg_over_c_tg:.4f}   (geometry prior 15.6/12 = 1.300)')
    print(f'  fit resid: rms {resid.std():.4f} V, max|{np.abs(resid).max():.4f}| V')
    print(f'  CNP Rxx range over good rows: {np.nanmin(rmax[good])/1e3:.1f}k .. {np.nanmax(rmax[good])/1e3:.1f}k')

# --- render both maps with sr1 ridge overlay ---
ext = [TGv.min(), TGv.max(), BGv.min(), BGv.max()]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 5))
for a, R, ttl in [(ax[0], R1, 'sr1 Rxx T3-T4'), (ax[1], R2, 'sr2 Rxx B4-B5'), (ax[2], R3, 'sr3 Rxy T5-B6')]:
    im = a.imshow(R/1e3, origin='lower', aspect='auto', extent=ext,
                  cmap='viridis', vmin=0, vmax=np.nanpercentile(R/1e3, 99))
    a.set_xlabel('V_TG (V)'); a.set_ylabel('V_BG (V)'); a.set_title(ttl)
    plt.colorbar(im, ax=a, label='kOhm')
tg1, _, e1 = ridge(R1)
ax[0].plot(tg1[~e1], BGv[~e1], 'r.', ms=4, label='CNP ridge')
ax[0].plot(tg1[e1], BGv[e1], 'rx', ms=5, label='edge-clipped')
p1 = np.polyfit(BGv[~e1], tg1[~e1], 1)
ax[0].plot(np.polyval(p1, BGv), BGv, 'w--', lw=1, label=f'fit {p1[0]:+.2f}Vbg{p1[1]:+.2f}')
ax[0].legend(fontsize=7, loc='lower left')
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('hera_scratch/ana_gatemap.png', dpi=100)
print('\nsaved hera_scratch/ana_gatemap.png')

    tg = np.full(nBG, np.nan); rm = np.full(nBG, np.nan); edge = np.zeros(nBG, bool)

1	# Landau fan
2	
3	## What
4	2D map of carrier density × magnetic field at fixed displacement field: `mag.field` as the **slow** axis of a `multimegasweep`, with a paired-(k_tg, k_bg) n-line (fixed D, via `calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`) as the **fast** axis:
5	```python
6	s.multimegasweep([mag.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)
7	```
8	Field is slow because gates are cheap to retrace and the magnet is not — the magnet ramps once, monotonically, across the whole fan. Every lock-in X/P read at each grid point. Analysis side plots B vs n (`pcolormesh`) per contact pair and overlays Středa lines (see Verify). Distinct from its two neighbors: `field-sweep-1d` is one gate point with full B-axis density; `gatemap-in-field` is the full 2D gate plane at a *single* B. The fan trades both for the (n, B) plane — the only measurement that resolves how gapped states *disperse* with field.
9	
10	## When
11	Three triggers, in rough campaign order:
12	- **Oscillation check** — a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap-in-field` showed quantum-oscillation-like wiggles and you need to know if they're real. The corpus idiom is literally named for this: RPL_19's "Small fan to check if oscillations are real" (a 161 × 151 fan after an effective-mass series kept hinting at SdH). A feature that moves systematically across the n-line as B steps is physics; one that doesn't is noise or gate drift.
13	- **State classification** — a map shows a vanishing-ρxx region (or a busy set of dips) and the discriminating question is whether the features disperse. This is the classification backbone of an FQAH/SC-style campaign (arXiv 2504.06972: ρxx(ν_h, B) fans + Středa fits are how (R/F/I)QAH states were separated from the SC region).
14	- **Calibration** — SdH/LL frequency vs n gives cap ratios independently of the CNP-slope method, and for a moiré device the fan anchors the moiré density n_M. The extraction is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written); the fan is its input data.
15	
16	Prerequisites are `nD-map`'s plus a field-verified magnet: cap ratios `dtg`/`dbg` must be trusted (the fast axis is a line in (n, D) — wrong caps tilt it), and the field source must be live (Yokogawa cache seeded after kernel restart, AMI430 in operating mode — see `field-sweep-1d` plumbing notes).
17	
18	## Why
19	A dip in ρxx at one B value is ambiguous — gap, SC, contact artifact, density wobble. The same dip tracked across a fan is nearly unambiguous: a gapped state at fixed filling traces a straight line in (n, B) whose slope *is* its Chern number (Středa: dn/dB = C·e/h), an SC pocket sits at fixed n and dies at moderate B without dispersing, and quantum oscillations fan out with 1/B periodicity that yields the Fermi-surface area. One measurement, three discriminations, plus calibration for free.
20	
21	The cost is real: these are the most expensive sweeps in the corpus. Reference wall-clocks *(our-measurement, toploader, non-blocking-magnet era — the formula below them omits the traverse term; do not carry these numbers to another rig untagged)*: RPL_10's 101 B × 101 n fan at `slow_delay=30, fast_delay=1` took **4.3 h** (file 156); the 351 × 251 version took **27.8 h** (file 159); RPL_19's 161 × 151 at `fast_delay=0.6` took **5.5 h** (file 1776 — Aaron's own `# 1776, took 5.5 hours` annotation propagates through later fan cells); the 441 × 231 fan to 5 T took **30.1 h** (file 1840). Aaron's inline arithmetic (`(351*501)/(201*151)*3` in 20260124 cell 134) is the toploader-era form.
22	
23	**Estimate before you run — the full cost model**: wall-clock = **field-traverse time + N_rows × (row turnaround + N_fast × per-point time)**. Which term dominates is a rig property, not a constant of nature: **if the field source is ramp-rate-limited and the set call blocks** (check the rig card for whether yours is), the traverse term is fixed by the B-span alone — **finer B steps cost only row turnaround, and coarsening B buys aliasing, not time**. Traverses come in two species, priced differently: a **bare ramp** moves at the magnet's ramp rate; a **measured traverse** (the same leg recorded as a sweep) moves at an effective rate degraded by per-point overhead. A "free" measured ramp-down is usually still worth taking — it buys data for wall-clock — but it is not free: price it at the measured rate, from the rig card's Timing rules (`rig_card.md`), never the bare one. Calibrate row turnaround and per-point time from this session's own first sweeps; inherited timing constants carry a provenance tag and the conditions they were measured under, or they are guesses.
24	
25	## Recipe
26	1. Pick the n-window and fixed D from the map that motivated the fan, and decide the B span. Corpus shapes: oscillation check 0.9 → 2.5 T over a 151-pt n-line; classification fan 0 → 2.5 T, 251 × 151; deep fan 0.6 → 5 T, 441 × 231; high-field 5 → 12 T, 351 × 201. Start coarse (≤200 B steps, ≤151 n points); zoom only on confirmed structure. **Grid Nyquist check, both axes, at design time**: against the finest expected feature spacing in the analysis window — for SdH/LL structure the B-period at fixed n is ΔB ≈ (g·e/h)·B²/n (g = level degeneracy, 4 for spin×valley); evaluate at the **lowest-B, highest-n corner** of the hunt window and require ≥2 (prefer 3) rows per period, and the analogous check on the n-axis (ray spacing Δn = g·(e/h)·B at the lowest B you intend to read). An undersampled axis produces in-data aliasing that mimics curved structure and survives re-plotting; no post-hoc check fully recovers it. "Start coarse" applies to the *window*, never below the Nyquist floor of the structure you intend to claim — and where the cost model says fine B is nearly free (blocking ramp-limited magnets), take it. **Re-run this check whenever n_max changes — never inherit a ΔB across fans.** The B-period ΔB ∝ B²/n shrinks as n grows, so a ΔB that was Nyquist-OK for an n≤4 fan can undersample an n=10 firming fan at the same B (our-measurement, QC0426/VTI 2026-06-14: ΔB=0.1 T gave 2.2 rows/period at n=4 but only 1.5 — under the ≥2 floor — at n=10, B=4 T; the undersampled corner is exactly where a spurious high-n second pocket appeared and had to be killed post-hoc). Where the rig makes fine B *not* free (measurement-dominated fans, e.g. a non-blocking-magnet rig at >1 s/pt — check the cost model), buy the high-n Nyquist floor by **trimming n-points or flooring the high-n claim at B ≥ 5–6 T**, not by coarsening B.
27	2. Build the fast axis: `ns = np.linspace(n_hi, n_lo, N); Ds = D0 * np.ones(len(ns)); Vtgs, Vbgs = calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`. A non-uniform n-vector is legitimate when you know where the action is — RPL_19's elevated-T fan stitches `np.hstack((n1, n2, n3))` with the dense segment over the CSC window and coarse segments elsewhere, with `#`-comments labeling each segment (20260124 cell 239).
28	3. Set lock-in sensitivity and time constant *before* the fan — at high B the resistance scale can be 10–100× the zero-field value and autorange-mid-fan ruins row-to-row comparability. RPL_19/20260217 cell 124 is the idiom: `sr830_N.sensitivity(10e-3)`, `sr830_N.time_constant(300e-3)` as an explicit pre-cell. Excitation: Aaron runs 1 V (graphene-scale) and bumps to 2.5 V for 12 T work; on a fragile-state device (FQAH/SC, arXiv 2504.06972's 1 nA cap) respect the device-card excitation ceiling instead — the states you're classifying wash out if heated.
29	4. Position the magnet at the fan's start field and let it settle: `s.ramp(mag.field, B_start)` then `time.sleep(600)` for multi-tesla positioning (RPL_19/20260217 cells 88/94), `time.sleep(30)` at ~1 T (RPL_10), `time.sleep(5*60)` at 0.6 T (20260124 cell 235). Plan the direction so the fan *starts* where the magnet already is and *ends* where the next measurement needs it — never re-traverse. The elevated-T fan covers ±5 T as four chained segments (5→0.6, 0.6→0, 0→−0.6, −0.6→−5; 20260124 cells 239–242), each starting where the last ended. A descending non-uniform `field_vec = np.hstack((np.linspace(12, 3, 181), np.linspace(3, 0, 151)))` packs steps densely where LLs are closely spaced (20260217 cell 96).
30	5. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('landau-fan')` then a structured tag: `s.add_comment(f'D = {D0} V/nm, n = {n_lo} to {n_hi}, B = {B_start} to {B_end} T')`, plus `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` where available. **Watch out** — RPL_10's fans carry exemplary comments (`'MC4, Vsi = -20V, quantum oscillations, D = 0.31 V/nm, n = -2.9 to -2.1, B = 1 to 0 T'`); RPL_19's fan cells carry *none* (files 1776/1840 have empty `comments`) — only a stale `# 1776` Python comment. The recipe asks for the RPL_10 discipline.
31	6. `s.ramp(sr830_1.amplitude, A)`, `s.ramp(k_si.volt, V_si)`, `s.ramp(bias_voltage.volt, 0)` if present. `fp` temperature(s) and every lock-in X/P; `plot` gate currents for live leakage (`s.plot(k_bg.volt, k_bg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_tg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_si.curr)` — RPL_19 fan idiom; note `fp` of gate currents is often omitted here, so leakage lands in the live plot but *not* in the TSV).
32	7. The sweep (step 0 call above). Delay band in the corpus: `slow_delay=1` (gates retrace during it; the field step itself is rate-limited by the magnet), `fast_delay` 0.5–1.0 s matching the time-constant ladder.
33	8. Park gates (`k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)`), decide the field endpoint deliberately (leave it for a follow-up fan, `s.ramp(mag.field, 0)`, or ride home as a measured traverse — a free `field-sweep-1d`, priced at the measured rate per the Why cost model), and ping (`alerts.discord('🐍jobs done🐍')`) — at 5–30 h these runs outlive operator attention spans.
34	
35	## Verify
36	Disk-side checks, then the Středa read. The fan is unrolled into flat rows; the slow column is `magnet_field`.
37	
38	```python
39	from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run
40	import numpy as np
41	
42	run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
43	print(summarize_run(run))
44	# expect: type 2D, recipe 'landau-fan', slow_param ['magnet_field'],
45	#         fast_param ['k_tg_volt', 'k_bg_volt'].
46	
47	# 1. Completeness — at 5-30 h these are the most interruption-prone sweeps
48	#    in the corpus (RPL_10 file 158 and TD48-era runs died early; Aaron
49	#    re-ran rather than salvaged).
50	assert not run.interrupted, "fan was interrupted; decide re-run vs salvage with the human"
51	
52	# 2. B axis actually traversed the plan, monotonically per segment.
53	B = run.col("magnet_field")
54	print(f"B traversed: {B.min():.3f} → {B.max():.3f} T over {len(run.meta['slow_setpoints'][0])} steps")
55	
56	# 3. Fast axis is a paired n-line: both gate columns move together.
57	vtg, vbg = run.col("k_tg_volt"), run.col("k_bg_volt")
58	assert np.ptp(vtg) > 0 and np.ptp(vbg) > 0, "one gate is frozen — not a paired n-line"
59	
60	# 4. Temperature stayed at base across the fan (a 30 h run spans fridge
61	#    events). NOTE: 20260124-era RPL_19 data has TWO columns literally
62	#    named 'T' (probe + fridge); later sessions rename to T_probe/T_fridge.
63	#    run.col('T') raises on the duplicate — use col_indices/col_at.
64	for tname in ("T_probe", "T"):
65	    idxs = run.col_indices(tname)
66	    if idxs:
67	        T = run.col_at(idxs[0])
68	        print(f"{tname}: {np.nanmin(T)*1e3:.0f}–{np.nanmax(T)*1e3:.0f} mK")
69	        break
70	
71	# 5. Lock-ins not flat/NaN (same as gatemap). Gate-current columns are
72	#    usually ABSENT in fan data (plot-only, step 6) — skip, don't fail.
73	for name in set(run.cols):
74	    if name.startswith("sr830_") and name.endswith("_X"):
75	        x = run.col_at(run.col_indices(name)[0])
76	        if np.allclose(x, x[0]) or np.isnan(x).any():
77	            print(f"⚠️  {name} flat or NaN — check sensitivity/wiring")
78	```
79	
80	**Středa read** (the point of the fan): track ρxx dip positions n_dip(B) per B-row and fit dn/dB per dip family.
81	- A linearly dispersing dip is a gapped state with Chern number `C = (h/e) · dn/dB` (n in absolute units). The corpus tools are inline in the ana notebooks: `streda()` returning `B = phi0 * n / C` (RPL_19/20251220_ana cells 96–98) and the overlay form `x_fit = C * y_fit * 1E-16 / (h/e)` plotted over the file-1840 fan (20260124_ana cell 93, C = 1 dashed line with the constants from the boilerplate cell 3).
82	- **Moiré devices**: the slope converts to a Chern number only through the moiré density — `C = (h/e) · n_M · dν_h/dB`. The corpus has no ν_h layer; anchoring n_M and the ν_h↔n conversion is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written). Until it exists, report slopes in raw dn/dB and flag the assignment.
83	- **Do not hard-code "plateau value ⇒ Středa slope"** [flagged for expert review]: the RIQAH states in arXiv 2504.06972 show ρxy quantized at h/e² while their ρxx dips disperse with slopes near their *fractional filling*, not C = 1 — explicitly unexplained in that paper. A plateau/dispersion mismatch is an escalate-to-expert finding, not a fit error.
84	- **Fan onset as a quality metric**: the lowest B at which oscillations/LL dips resolve tracks quantum mobility — RPL_10's fans resolved structure below 1 T; RPL_19's oscillation check needed 0.9–2.5 T. A later cooldown whose onset field moves up is a device-quality regression worth noting.
85	
86	## Examples
87	- `aaron/RPL_10/241230_measure.ipynb` cells 50–53 — the original fans, exemplary comment discipline. **Cell-range adjustment vs. index**: the index synopsis lumps these under "n-vs-B sweeps at D = 0.31" (cells 49–53); within that, cell 51 is a strict 1D field sweep (claimed by `field-sweep-1d` Examples, which already flags 50/52/53 as "landau-fan-shaped") and cell 54 is a *raw, never-executed* draft fan at D = 0.25. The executed fans: cell 50 → file 156 (101 B × 101 n, B 1→0 T, `slow_delay=30, fast_delay=1`, 4.3 h), cell 52 → file 158 (351 × 201 — **interrupted at 0.0 h** and immediately superseded), cell 53 → file 159 (351 × 251, 27.8 h, the fan the qo-discovery fixture freezes on). Note B runs *downward* (1→0): the magnet was parked at 1 T by the preceding `## Gate maps in field` cells 46–48, so the fan starts where the magnet sits.
88	- `aaron/RPL_19/20260124_measure.ipynb` cells 117–119, 173–176, 234–242, 278–284 — the mature fan family. **Cell-range adjustment vs. index**: the brief cited the "Small fan to check if oscillations are real" as ~cells 167–176; actually 167–172 are still `# Resuming effective mass` (higher field range), the small-fan section is header 173, base-recool cell 174 (`heater.volt(0)` + 1 h `interruptable_sleep`), fans 175 (D = 0.2) and 176 (D = 1) — 161 B steps 0.9→2.5 T × 151-pt n-line, `fast_delay=0.6` → file 1776, 5.5 h, the `after-qo-confirmed` fixture cut. Cell 119 is the first `## Test fan` (501 × 51, B 0.75–1.25 T at 1 mT steps). Cells 234–242 are the deep fan (cell 236 → file 1840: 441 × 231, 0.6→5 T, 30.1 h) plus the `## Elevated T Fan` (heater at 2.75 V, 20-min settle, designer hstack n-vector, ±5 T in four chained segments). Cells 280–283 (`# Landau fans`) repeat a 251 × 151 shape across D = 1.04/0.95/0.9/0.25 — a D-ladder of fans, each cell differing only in `ns`/`Ds` and sweep direction (alternating 2.5→0 / 0→2.5 so consecutive fans never re-traverse). No `add_comment` in any of these — see Recipe step 5.
89	- `aaron/RPL_19/20260217_measure.ipynb` cells 87–96 and 123–126 — fans with explicit field-settle and lock-in-setup cells. Cells 88/91/94 are `s.ramp(mag.field, B); time.sleep(600)` positioning cells; cell 89 presets sensitivity; cells 90/92 are 201 × 101 CSC fans at D = 1.02/0.98 (2.5→0.5 T); cell 95 is the 12 T fan (5→12 T, 351 × 201); cell 96 descends 12→0 with the two-density hstack `field_vec`. 90	
91	## Next
92	- **Oscillations confirmed real**: two branches, both exercised in RPL_19/20260124 — (a) `field-sweep-1d` cuts at fixed (n, D) with high B-density to read the SdH frequency cleanly (`# Cuts at fixed n and D`, cell 177 — the `after-qo-confirmed` fixture's contested decision), and (b) an effective-mass temperature series: repeat one field sweep at a heater ladder and fit amplitude vs T — that is `temperature-dependence` Flavor B.
93	- **Dips disperse linearly**: (F/I)QAH-family candidate with C from the slope. Cross-check the Hall channel for the matching plateau; if plateau and slope disagree, escalate (RIQAH caution above). Assigning ν requires n_M — `cap-ratio-calibration` (deferred).
94	- **A vanishing-ρxx region does NOT disperse and dies at moderate B**: SC candidate. Next: `field-sweep-1d` fine B-scans at the region's center (critical field, ±mT hygiene), `hysteresis-check` for switching, and dV/dI vs I_dc when `bias-spectroscopy` exists (deferred) — cf. arXiv 2504.06972's SC dome (B_c ≈ 0.6–0.8 T).
95	- **Fan looks streaky / row-to-row jumps**: sensitivity changed mid-fan (autorange left on) or the magnet didn't settle. Re-run with the step-3 preset cell and a longer step-4 settle.
96	- **Caps or n_M wanted from this fan**: `cap-ratio-calibration` (deferred) — the SdH-frequency method; until written, the extraction is ana-side judgment (cf. the QO FFT pipeline, RPL_19/20260112_ana cell 125).
97	- **Fan at one D is interesting**: D-ladder of fans (20260124 cells 280–283 idiom) or an `Elevated T Fan` to see which features survive warming — `temperature-dependence` decides the ladder.

2. Build the fast axis: `ns = np.linspace(n_hi, n_lo, N); Ds = D0 * np.ones(len(ns)); Vtgs, Vbgs = calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`. A non-uniform n-vector is legitimate when you know where the action is — RPL_19's elevated-T fan stitches `np.hstack((n1, n2, n3))` with the dense segment over the CSC window and coarse segments elsewhere, with `#`-comments labeling each segment (20260124 cell 239).
3. Set lock-in sensitivity and time constant *before* the fan — at high B the resistance scale can be 10–100× the zero-field value and autorange-mid-fan ruins row-to-row comparability. RPL_19/20260217 cell 124 is the idiom: `sr830_N.sensitivity(10e-3)`, `sr830_N.time_constant(300e-3)` as an explicit pre-cell. Excitation: Aaron runs 1 V (graphene-scale) and bumps to 2.5 V for 12 T work; on a fragile-state device (FQAH/SC, arXiv 2504.06972's 1 nA cap) respect the device-card excitation ceiling instead — the states you're classifying wash out if heated.
4. Position the magnet at the fan's start field and let it settle: `s.ramp(mag.field, B_start)` then `time.sleep(600)` for multi-tesla positioning (RPL_19/20260217 cells 88/94), `time.sleep(30)` at ~1 T (RPL_10), `time.sleep(5*60)` at 0.6 T (20260124 cell 235). Plan the direction so the fan *starts* where the magnet already is and *ends* where the next measurement needs it — never re-traverse. The elevated-T fan covers ±5 T as four chained segments (5→0.6, 0.6→0, 0→−0.6, −0.6→−5; 20260124 cells 239–242), each starting where the last ended. A descending non-uniform `field_vec = np.hstack((np.linspace(12, 3, 181), np.linspace(3, 0, 151)))` packs steps densely where LLs are closely spaced (20260217 cell 96).
5. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('landau-fan')` then a structured tag: `s.add_comment(f'D = {D0} V/nm, n = {n_lo} to {n_hi}, B = {B_start} to {B_end} T')`, plus `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` where available. **Watch out** — RPL_10's fans carry exemplary comments (`'MC4, Vsi = -20V, quantum oscillations, D = 0.31 V/nm, n = -2.9 to -2.1, B = 1 to 0 T'`); RPL_19's fan cells carry *none* (files 1776/1840 have empty `comments`) — only a stale `# 1776` Python comment. The recipe asks for the RPL_10 discipline.
6. `s.ramp(sr830_1.amplitude, A)`, `s.ramp(k_si.volt, V_si)`, `s.ramp(bias_voltage.volt, 0)` if present. `fp` temperature(s) and every lock-in X/P; `plot` gate currents for live leakage (`s.plot(k_bg.volt, k_bg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_tg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_si.curr)` — RPL_19 fan idiom; note `fp` of gate currents is often omitted here, so leakage lands in the live plot but *not* in the TSV).
7. The sweep (step 0 call above). Delay band in the corpus: `slow_delay=1` (gates retrace during it; the field step itself is rate-limited by the magnet), `fast_delay` 0.5–1.0 s matching the time-constant ladder.

"""SdH spot-check analysis. Usage: menv python sdh_analyze.py <run_id> <n_cm2> [onset_T]
Per-channel: raw Rxx(B), 5th-order background subtract, onset read, FFT in 1/B vs F_L,
peak set + Luttinger combinatorics, FFT-stability sweep (detrend/window)."""
import sys, json, numpy as np
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_fft, luttinger_frequency

run_id = sys.argv[1]; n_cm = float(sys.argv[2]); onset = float(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else None
r = open_run(f'data/{run_id}')
m = json.load(open(f'data/{run_id}/metadata.json'))
Ib = m['measurement_config']['bias_voltage'] / m['measurement_config']['bias_resistor']
B = r.col('magnet_mag')
order = np.argsort(B); B = B[order]
chans = {'sr1 T3-T4': 'sr1_X', 'sr2 B4-B5': 'sr2_X'}
FL = luttinger_frequency(abs(n_cm) * 1e4)   # n in m^-2
print(f'run {run_id}: n={n_cm:+.1e} cm^-2, F_L={FL:.1f} T, B {B.min():.3f}..{B.max():.3f} T, npts={len(B)}')

fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(chans), 3, figsize=(16, 4.2 * len(chans)))
if len(chans) == 1: axes = axes[None, :]
for i, (nm, col) in enumerate(chans.items()):
    R = (r.col(col) / Ib)[order]
    # background subtract (5th order) for onset + raw oscillation view
    p = np.polyfit(B, R, 5); dR = R - np.polyval(p, B)
    a0, a1, a2 = axes[i]
    a0.plot(B, R, lw=.8); a0.set_title(f'{nm}  Rxx(B)'); a0.set_xlabel('B (T)'); a0.set_ylabel('Rxx (ohm)'); a0.grid(alpha=.3)
    a1.plot(B, dR, lw=.8); a1.set_title('dRxx (5th-order bkg removed)'); a1.set_xlabel('B (T)'); a1.grid(alpha=.3)
    if onset: a1.axvline(onset, color='r', ls='--', lw=1, label=f'onset {onset}T'); a1.legend(fontsize=8)
    # FFT over [onset, Bmax]; stability sweep over detrend + window
    blo = onset if onset else max(B.min(), 0.5)
    for det, win, lab in [(5, 'hann', 'd5 hann'), (3, 'hann', 'd3 hann'), (5, 'blackman', 'd5 black')]:
        f, S = sdh_fft(R, B, b_range=(blo, B.max()), detrend=det, window=win, nfft=2048, log=False)
        a2.plot(f, S / np.nanmax(S), lw=.9, label=lab)
    a2.axvline(FL, color='k', ls='--', lw=1, label=f'F_L={FL:.0f}T')
    a2.axvline(FL / 2, color='gray', ls=':', lw=1, label='F_L/2')
    a2.set_xlim(0, FL * 1.6); a2.set_title('FFT in 1/B (stability sweep)'); a2.set_xlabel('F (T)'); a2.legend(fontsize=7); a2.grid(alpha=.3)
    # report peaks (on d5/hann)
    f, S = sdh_fft(R, B, b_range=(blo, B.max()), detrend=5, window='hann', nfft=2048, log=False)
    band = (f > 3) & (f < FL * 1.5)
    fb, Sb = f[band], S[band]
    from scipy.signal import find_peaks
    pk, _ = find_peaks(Sb, height=0.15 * Sb.max(), distance=10)
    pk = pk[np.argsort(Sb[pk])[::-1]][:6]
    print(f'  [{nm}] onset~{blo}T  peaks (T): ' +
          ', '.join(f'{fb[k]:.1f}({Sb[k]/Sb.max():.2f})' for k in pk) +
          f'  | F_L={FL:.1f}  F_L/2={FL/2:.1f}')
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig(f'hera_scratch/sdh_{run_id}.png', dpi=100)
print(f'saved hera_scratch/sdh_{run_id}.png')

def sdh_fft(
    R_grid: np.ndarray,
    B: np.ndarray,
    *,
    b_range: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    nfft: int = 512,
    detrend: int | None = 3,
    window: str | None = "hann",
    log: bool = True,
    floor: float = 1.0,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Per-column Shubnikov–de Haas FFT in 1/B.

    `R_grid` is `(n_B, n_fast)` (rows = field, the `FanGrids` row axis); `B`
    is the per-row field `(n_B,)`. For each column: select `b_range`, resample
    onto a regular `nfft`-point 1/B grid (interpolating against **sorted** 1/B
    — B descends in a come-down fan), optionally `log10(max(R, floor))`,
    polynomial-`detrend`, `window`, then rFFT.

    Returns `(freqs, spec)` — `freqs` in Tesla `(n_freq,)`, `spec` the FFT
    magnitude `(n_fast, n_freq)`.
    """
    B = np.asarray(B, dtype=float)
    R_grid = np.asarray(R_grid, dtype=float)
    if R_grid.shape[0] != B.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError(f"R_grid rows {R_grid.shape[0]} != len(B) {B.shape[0]}")
    sel = np.ones(B.shape, dtype=bool) if b_range is None else (B >= b_range[0]) & (B <= b_range[1])
    if sel.sum() < 4:
        raise ValueError(f"need >=4 field rows in b_range; got {int(sel.sum())}")
    invB = 1.0 / B[sel]
    order = np.argsort(invB)
    invB_sorted = invB[order]
    u = np.linspace(invB_sorted[0], invB_sorted[-1], nfft)
    du = u[1] - u[0]
    freqs = np.fft.rfftfreq(nfft, du)  # Tesla
    win = _window(window, nfft)
    spec = np.zeros((R_grid.shape[1], freqs.size))
    for j in range(R_grid.shape[1]):
        y = R_grid[sel, j]
        if log:
            y = np.log10(np.maximum(y, floor))
        yi = np.interp(u, invB_sorted, y[order])
        if detrend is not None:
            yi = yi - np.polyval(np.polyfit(u, yi, detrend), u)
        spec[j] = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(yi * win))
    return freqs, spec

"""SdH spot-check analysis. Usage: menv python sdh_analyze.py <run_id> <n_cm2> [onset_T]
Per-channel: raw Rxx(B), 5th-order background subtract, onset read, FFT in 1/B vs F_L,
peak set + Luttinger combinatorics, FFT-stability sweep (detrend/window)."""
import sys, json, numpy as np
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_fft, luttinger_frequency

run_id = sys.argv[1]; n_cm = float(sys.argv[2]); onset = float(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else None
r = open_run(f'data/{run_id}')
m = json.load(open(f'data/{run_id}/metadata.json'))
Ib = m['measurement_config']['bias_voltage'] / m['measurement_config']['bias_resistor']
B = r.col('magnet_mag')
order = np.argsort(B); B = B[order]
chans = {'sr1 T3-T4': 'sr1_X', 'sr2 B4-B5': 'sr2_X'}
FL = luttinger_frequency(abs(n_cm) * 1e4)   # n in m^-2
print(f'run {run_id}: n={n_cm:+.1e} cm^-2, F_L={FL:.1f} T, B {B.min():.3f}..{B.max():.3f} T, npts={len(B)}')

fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(chans), 3, figsize=(16, 4.2 * len(chans)))
if len(chans) == 1: axes = axes[None, :]
for i, (nm, col) in enumerate(chans.items()):
    R = (r.col(col) / Ib)[order]
    # background subtract (5th order) for onset + raw oscillation view
    p = np.polyfit(B, R, 5); dR = R - np.polyval(p, B)
    a0, a1, a2 = axes[i]
    a0.plot(B, R, lw=.8); a0.set_title(f'{nm}  Rxx(B)'); a0.set_xlabel('B (T)'); a0.set_ylabel('Rxx (ohm)'); a0.grid(alpha=.3)
    a1.plot(B, dR, lw=.8); a1.set_title('dRxx (5th-order bkg removed)'); a1.set_xlabel('B (T)'); a1.grid(alpha=.3)
    if onset: a1.axvline(onset, color='r', ls='--', lw=1, label=f'onset {onset}T'); a1.legend(fontsize=8)
    # FFT over [onset, Bmax]; stability sweep over detrend + window
    blo = onset if onset else max(B.min(), 0.5)
    for det, win, lab in [(5, 'hann', 'd5 hann'), (3, 'hann', 'd3 hann'), (5, 'blackman', 'd5 black')]:
        f, S = sdh_fft(R, B, b_range=(blo, B.max()), detrend=det, window=win, nfft=2048, log=False)
        a2.plot(f, S / np.nanmax(S), lw=.9, label=lab)
    a2.axvline(FL, color='k', ls='--', lw=1, label=f'F_L={FL:.0f}T')
    a2.axvline(FL / 2, color='gray', ls=':', lw=1, label='F_L/2')
    a2.set_xlim(0, FL * 1.6); a2.set_title('FFT in 1/B (stability sweep)'); a2.set_xlabel('F (T)'); a2.legend(fontsize=7); a2.grid(alpha=.3)
    # report peaks (on d5/hann)
    f, S = sdh_fft(R, B, b_range=(blo, B.max()), detrend=5, window='hann', nfft=2048, log=False)
    band = (f > 3) & (f < FL * 1.5)
    fb, Sb = f[band], S[band]
    from scipy.signal import find_peaks
    pk, _ = find_peaks(Sb, height=0.15 * Sb.max(), distance=10)
    pk = pk[np.argsort(Sb[pk])[::-1]][:6]
    print(f'  [{nm}] onset~{blo}T  peaks (T): ' +
          ', '.join(f'{fb[k]:.1f}({Sb[k]/Sb.max():.2f})' for k in pk) +
          f'  | F_L={FL:.1f}  F_L/2={FL/2:.1f}')
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig(f'hera_scratch/sdh_{run_id}.png', dpi=100)
print(f'saved hera_scratch/sdh_{run_id}.png')

Operational log (RECIPE FIX / TOOLING / PROTOCOL / FEEDBACK). Not a science notebook —
points at data/cells/recipes, does not duplicate them.

## Bring-up (E0)

- Gate A green: magnet (field 0.002 T, output enabled, PS heater on), LS335 sample

  exactly (TG [-6,+7], BG [-4.5,+4.5], Si [-50,+50]) and B cap 8.0 T on magnet.mag.vals

## GRANT — E1 engaged 2026-06-17

Operator (callsign "alpha sierra") gave **"go for autonomy"**. E1 active. First E1
execute = read-only kernel-binding probe (measure cell 28). Re-entry after any E0
drop requires a fresh explicit grant.

## RECIPE FIX / PROTOCOL — never fp(heater.sample_temperature) in a VTI sweep

Gate C liveness (measure cell 30, exec 16) **errored at point 0** with VisaIOError
TMO on `KRDG? A` (`heater.sample_temperature`). Root cause = the rig-card "LS335 has
two masters" quirk: per-point polling of the Lakeshore contends with the Grafana
logger and times out. Fix: do **not** `s.fp(heater.sample_temperature)` (or any
LS335 read) inside the per-point loop — record T once in `meas_config` (snapshot)
and lean on the Grafana log (timestamped) for any post-hoc T(t)/T(B) correction.
Applies to gate map + fans too. Run id 0 = the dud (metadata only, 0 rows).
gate-current-sanity-check.md fps `temperature` per point — fine on toploader, a trap
on VTI; the recipe should carry a VTI caveat. Corrected liveness re-run as a new cell.

## Gate C PASS (run 1) + gate map launched (run 2)

- Gate C liveness (measure cell 32, run 1): device alive — drain I flat 5.0 nA
  (current-bias OK), Rxx modulates (peak ~1.4k @ V_TG~0 at BG=0), sr1/sr2 corr 0.99
  but not identical (no grounded short), leakage floor (BG 35 pA, Si 0.57 nA on 1uA
  range). Promoted to ana cell 11. **Device R is LOW (~kohm)** -> my 5 mV sens
  over-coarsened (47.7 ohm quantization); using 0.5 mV for the map.
- OBSERVATION: the single TG trace shows a **double-peak** near V_TG 0 and +0.45,
  **common to both Rxx channels** (same V positions) -> a real feature in the gate
  response, not a per-contact mosaic CNP offset. Resolve in the 2D map (could be a
  two-CNP / low-density band feature; far too early to interpret).
- Gate map (measure cell 34, run 2): 0T BG[-4.5,4.5]x25 x TG[-6,6]x61, Si=0, sens
  0.5 mV. Launched bg; ~50-60 min; row-12 health checkpoint armed via hera-watch.
- DESIGN NOTE: TG=DC205 -> sweep `dc205_volt` (col DC_bias), NOT k_tg.volt. landau-
  fan-vti.md says fast axis `[k_tg.volt,k_bg.volt]` (generic) — for QC0426 substitute
  `[dc205_volt, k_bg.volt]`. dc205_volt has NO get -> never s.ramp it; park via set.

## CNP / (n,D) calibration — ESTABLISHED (run 2, ana cells 12-13)

- CNP line per channel: sr1 (T3-T4) Vtg=-1.305*Vbg+0.174; sr2 (B4-B5) Vtg=-1.298*Vbg

import numpy as np, json
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_fft, luttinger_frequency

r = open_run('data/4')
m = json.load(open('data/4/metadata.json'))
Ib = m['measurement_config']['bias_voltage'] / m['measurement_config']['bias_resistor']
B = r.col('magnet_mag'); o = np.argsort(B); B = B[o]
R = {'sr1 T3-T4': (r.col('sr1_X') / Ib)[o], 'sr2 B4-B5': (r.col('sr2_X') / Ib)[o]}
bmax = {'sr1 T3-T4': 5.3, 'sr2 B4-B5': 8.0}      # sr1 overloads >5.44T
FL = luttinger_frequency(8e16)                    # n=+8e12 cm^-2
ONSET = 2.0
print(f'n=+8e12, F_L={FL:.1f} T, F_L/2={FL/2:.1f} T')

fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(16, 8))
for i, (nm, Rc) in enumerate(R.items()):
    bm = bmax[nm]; sel = B <= bm
    Bc, Rc2 = B[sel], Rc[sel]
    p = np.polyfit(Bc, Rc2, 5); dR = Rc2 - np.polyval(p, Bc)
    ax[i, 0].plot(B, Rc, lw=.7); ax[i, 0].axvline(bm, color='r', ls=':', label=f'sr1 ovld {bm}T' if i == 0 else f'use<{bm}T')
    ax[i, 0].set_title(f'{nm} Rxx(B)'); ax[i, 0].set_ylabel('Rxx (ohm)'); ax[i, 0].grid(alpha=.3); ax[i, 0].legend(fontsize=7)
    ax[i, 1].plot(Bc, dR, lw=.8); ax[i, 1].axvline(ONSET, color='g', ls='--', label=f'onset {ONSET}T')
    ax[i, 1].set_title(f'{nm} dRxx (bkg removed)'); ax[i, 1].grid(alpha=.3); ax[i, 1].legend(fontsize=7)
    # FFT + stability sweep over [onset, bm]
    for det, win, lab in [(5, 'hann', 'd5 hann'), (3, 'hann', 'd3 hann'), (5, 'blackman', 'd5 black')]:
        f, Sg = sdh_fft(Rc.reshape(-1, 1), B, b_range=(ONSET, bm), detrend=det, window=win, nfft=4096, log=False)
        S = Sg[0]; ax[i, 2].plot(f, S / np.nanmax(S), lw=.9, label=lab)
    ax[i, 2].axvline(FL, color='k', ls='--', lw=1, label=f'F_L={FL:.0f}')
    ax[i, 2].axvline(FL/2, color='gray', ls=':', label='F_L/2')
    ax[i, 2].set_xlim(0, FL*1.5); ax[i, 2].set_title(f'{nm} FFT in 1/B [{ONSET}-{bm}T]'); ax[i, 2].set_xlabel('F (T)')
    ax[i, 2].legend(fontsize=7); ax[i, 2].grid(alpha=.3)
    # peaks (d5 hann)
    f, Sg = sdh_fft(Rc.reshape(-1, 1), B, b_range=(ONSET, bm), detrend=5, window='hann', nfft=4096, log=False)
    S = Sg[0]; band = (f > 4) & (f < FL*1.4); fb, Sb = f[band], S[band]
    pk, _ = find_peaks(Sb, height=0.12*Sb.max(), distance=8)
    pk = pk[np.argsort(Sb[pk])[::-1]][:6]
    pks = sorted(fb[k] for k in pk)
    print(f'[{nm}] B[{ONSET},{bm}] dF={1/(1/ONSET-1/bm):.1f}T  peaks(T): ' +
          ', '.join(f'{fb[k]:.1f}({Sb[k]/Sb.max():.2f})' for k in pk[np.argsort(fb[pk])]))
    print(f'    sum-check: pairs summing to F_L={FL:.0f}? ' +
          ', '.join(f'{a:.0f}+{b:.0f}={a+b:.0f}' for ii,a in enumerate(pks) for b in pks[ii+1:] if abs(a+b-FL)<8))
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig('hera_scratch/ana_spotA.png', dpi=100)
print('saved hera_scratch/ana_spotA.png')

print(f'F_L: gate(n=8.0e12)={FL_gate:.1f} T, Hall(n=8.4e12)={FL_hall:.1f} T')

    ax[i,1].set_title(f'{nm}  dRxx (5th-order bkg removed)'); ax[i,1].grid(alpha=.3); ax[i,1].legend(fontsize=7)

    ax[i,2].axvline(FL_gate, color='k', ls='--', label=f'F_L gate {FL_gate:.0f}')
    ax[i,2].axvline(FL_hall, color='b', ls='-.', label=f'F_L Hall {FL_hall:.0f}')

    ax[i,2].legend(fontsize=7); ax[i,2].grid(alpha=.3)
    f, Sg = sdh_fft(Rc.reshape(-1,1), B4, b_range=(ONSET, bm), detrend=5, window='hann', nfft=4096, log=False)

def multimegasweep(
        self,
        slow_params: list[Parameter],
        slow_v_list: list[Setpoints],
        fast_params: list[Parameter],
        fast_v_list: list[Setpoints],
        slow_delay: float = 0.0,
        fast_delay: float = 0.0,
        init_delay: bool = True,
    ) -> SweepResult:
        self._check_interrupted()
        if not all(len(sp) == len(fast_v_list[0]) for sp in fast_v_list):
            raise ValueError("not all fast axis setpoint lists have same length!")
        if not all(len(sp) == len(slow_v_list[0]) for sp in slow_v_list):
            raise ValueError("not all slow axis setpoint lists have same length!")

        slow_vs = [list(i) for i in zip(*slow_v_list)]
        fast_vs = [list(i) for i in zip(*fast_v_list)]

        with (
            self._sweep_context(),
            sweep.db.Writer(self._basedir) as w,
            self._plotter as p,
        ):
            self.logger.info(f"Starting multimegasweep with ID {w.id}")
            slowparamlist: list[str] = []
            for param in slow_params:
                slowparamlist.append(param.full_name)

            fastparamlist: list[str] = []
            for param in fast_params:
                fastparamlist.append(param.full_name)

            self.logger.debug(f"Slows: {slowparamlist}, Fasts: {fastparamlist}")
            min_duration = (
                len(slow_vs) * len(fast_vs) * fast_delay + len(slow_vs) * slow_delay
            )
            self.logger.info(f"Minimum duration {_sec_to_str(min_duration)}")

import sys, json, numpy as np
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg'); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_fft, luttinger_frequency
from scipy.signal import find_peaks

ONSET = float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 2.0
r = open_run('data/6'); m = json.load(open('data/6/metadata.json')); ci = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(m['columns'])}
raw = np.loadtxt('data/6/data.tsv.gz'); Ib = m['measurement_config']['bias_voltage'] / m['measurement_config']['bias_resistor']
Bcol = raw[:, ci['magnet_mag']]; Bvals = np.unique(Bcol); NB = len(Bvals)
ns_cm = np.linspace(2e12, 10e12, 33); NN = len(ns_cm)
print(f'fan: {len(raw)} pts -> {NB} B-rows x {NN} n-cols (expect {NB*NN})')
# reshape: rows ordered slow(B)-major, fast(n)-minor
def grid(col):
    g = (raw[:, ci[col]] / Ib)
    return g[:NB*NN].reshape(NB, NN)   # (B, n)
R1 = grid('sr1_X'); R2 = grid('sr2_X')
FLn = luttinger_frequency(ns_cm * 1e4)   # F_L(n), Tesla

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(17, 9))
for row, (nm, Rg) in enumerate([('sr1 T3-T4', R1), ('sr2 B4-B5', R2)]):
    # raw 2D Rxx(n,B)
    ax = axes[row, 0]
    im = ax.pcolormesh(ns_cm/1e12, Bvals, Rg, shading='auto', cmap='viridis')
    ax.set_xlabel('n (1e12 cm^-2)'); ax.set_ylabel('B (T)'); ax.set_title(f'{nm} Rxx(n,B)'); plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
    # per-column FFT (sdh_fft does all columns at once)
    f, spec = sdh_fft(Rg, Bvals, b_range=(ONSET, 8.0), detrend=5, window='hann', nfft=4096, log=False)
    fb = (f > 4) & (f < 120); fbf = f[fb]
    ax = axes[row, 1]
    Snorm = spec[:, fb] / spec[:, fb].max(axis=1, keepdims=True)   # normalize per column
    im = ax.pcolormesh(ns_cm/1e12, fbf, Snorm.T, shading='auto', cmap='magma')
    ax.plot(ns_cm/1e12, FLn, 'c--', lw=1.5, label='F_L(n)')
    ax.plot(ns_cm/1e12, FLn/2, 'c:', lw=1, label='F_L/2')
    ax.set_xlabel('n (1e12 cm^-2)'); ax.set_ylabel('F (T)'); ax.set_ylim(0, 115)
    ax.set_title(f'{nm} per-column FFT waterfall'); ax.legend(fontsize=7); plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
    # extract two branches per column: strongest peak in low band (<F_L/2) and high band
    fML, fBL = np.full(NN, np.nan), np.full(NN, np.nan)
    for j in range(NN):
        S = spec[j, fb]
        lo = fbf < FLn[j]*0.55; hi = (fbf >= FLn[j]*0.55) & (fbf < FLn[j]*1.25)
        if lo.sum() and S[lo].max() > 0.15*S.max():
            fML[j] = fbf[lo][np.argmax(S[lo])]
        if hi.sum() and S[hi].max() > 0.15*S.max():
            fBL[j] = fbf[hi][np.argmax(S[hi])]
    ax = axes[row, 2]
    ax.plot(ns_cm/1e12, fML, 'o-', ms=3, label='f_ML (low)')
    ax.plot(ns_cm/1e12, fBL, 's-', ms=3, label='f_BL (high)')
    ax.plot(ns_cm/1e12, fML+fBL, '^-', ms=3, label='f_ML+f_BL')
    ax.plot(ns_cm/1e12, FLn, 'k--', lw=1.5, label='F_L(n)')
    ax.set_xlabel('n (1e12 cm^-2)'); ax.set_ylabel('F (T)'); ax.set_title(f'{nm} partition test'); ax.legend(fontsize=7); ax.grid(alpha=.3)
    # numeric partition check (mid-high n where tones resolve)
    ok = np.isfinite(fML) & np.isfinite(fBL) & (ns_cm > 4e12)
    if ok.sum():
        resid = (fML[ok]+fBL[ok]-FLn[ok]) / FLn[ok]
        print(f'[{nm}] partition f_ML+f_BL vs F_L (n>4e12, {ok.sum()} cols): '
              f'mean resid {resid.mean()*100:+.1f}%, rms {resid.std()*100:.1f}% '
              f'| f_ML {np.nanmin(fML[ok]):.0f}-{np.nanmax(fML[ok]):.0f}T, f_BL {np.nanmin(fBL[ok]):.0f}-{np.nanmax(fBL[ok]):.0f}T')
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig('hera_scratch/fan_analyze.png', dpi=95)
print('saved hera_scratch/fan_analyze.png')
print('READ: two branches tracking with n, summing to F_L(n) across density = ABA')
print('(partition robust, model-independent). A single branch on F_L would be ABC.')

"""Electron fan (run 6) analysis: per-column SdH FFT -> F(n) branches -> the
partition-robustness test f_ML(n)+f_BL(n)=F_L(n), plus harmonic/intermod screen.
Run when the fan completes: menv python fan_analyze.py [onset]"""
import sys, json, numpy as np
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg'); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_fft, luttinger_frequency
from scipy.signal import find_peaks

ONSET = float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 2.0
r = open_run('data/6'); m = json.load(open('data/6/metadata.json')); ci = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(m['columns'])}
raw = np.loadtxt('data/6/data.tsv.gz'); Ib = m['measurement_config']['bias_voltage'] / m['measurement_config']['bias_resistor']
Bcol = raw[:, ci['magnet_mag']]; Bvals = np.unique(Bcol); NB = len(Bvals)
ns_cm = np.linspace(2e12, 10e12, 33); NN = len(ns_cm)
print(f'fan: {len(raw)} pts -> {NB} B-rows x {NN} n-cols (expect {NB*NN})')
# reshape: rows ordered slow(B)-major, fast(n)-minor
def grid(col):
    g = (raw[:, ci[col]] / Ib)
    return g[:NB*NN].reshape(NB, NN)   # (B, n)
R1 = grid('sr1_X'); R2 = grid('sr2_X')
FLn = luttinger_frequency(ns_cm * 1e4)   # F_L(n), Tesla

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(17, 9))
for row, (nm, Rg) in enumerate([('sr1 T3-T4', R1), ('sr2 B4-B5', R2)]):
    # raw 2D Rxx(n,B)
    ax = axes[row, 0]
    im = ax.pcolormesh(ns_cm/1e12, Bvals, Rg, shading='auto', cmap='viridis')
    ax.set_xlabel('n (1e12 cm^-2)'); ax.set_ylabel('B (T)'); ax.set_title(f'{nm} Rxx(n,B)'); plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
    # per-column FFT (sdh_fft does all columns at once)
    f, spec = sdh_fft(Rg, Bvals, b_range=(ONSET, 8.0), detrend=5, window='hann', nfft=4096, log=False)
    fb = (f > 4) & (f < 120); fbf = f[fb]
    ax = axes[row, 1]
    Snorm = spec[:, fb] / spec[:, fb].max(axis=1, keepdims=True)   # normalize per column
    im = ax.pcolormesh(ns_cm/1e12, fbf, Snorm.T, shading='auto', cmap='magma')
    ax.plot(ns_cm/1e12, FLn, 'c--', lw=1.5, label='F_L(n)')
    ax.plot(ns_cm/1e12, FLn/2, 'c:', lw=1, label='F_L/2')
    ax.set_xlabel('n (1e12 cm^-2)'); ax.set_ylabel('F (T)'); ax.set_ylim(0, 115)
    ax.set_title(f'{nm} per-column FFT waterfall'); ax.legend(fontsize=7); plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
    # extract two branches per column: strongest peak in low band (<F_L/2) and high band
    fML, fBL = np.full(NN, np.nan), np.full(NN, np.nan)
    for j in range(NN):
        S = spec[j, fb]
        lo = fbf < FLn[j]*0.55; hi = (fbf >= FLn[j]*0.55) & (fbf < FLn[j]*1.25)
        if lo.sum() and S[lo].max() > 0.15*S.max():
            fML[j] = fbf[lo][np.argmax(S[lo])]
        if hi.sum() and S[hi].max() > 0.15*S.max():
            fBL[j] = fbf[hi][np.argmax(S[hi])]
    ax = axes[row, 2]
    ax.plot(ns_cm/1e12, fML, 'o-', ms=3, label='f_ML (low)')
    ax.plot(ns_cm/1e12, fBL, 's-', ms=3, label='f_BL (high)')
    ax.plot(ns_cm/1e12, fML+fBL, '^-', ms=3, label='f_ML+f_BL')
    ax.plot(ns_cm/1e12, FLn, 'k--', lw=1.5, label='F_L(n)')
    ax.set_xlabel('n (1e12 cm^-2)'); ax.set_ylabel('F (T)'); ax.set_title(f'{nm} partition test'); ax.legend(fontsize=7); ax.grid(alpha=.3)
    # numeric partition check (mid-high n where tones resolve)
    ok = np.isfinite(fML) & np.isfinite(fBL) & (ns_cm > 4e12)
    if ok.sum():
        resid = (fML[ok]+fBL[ok]-FLn[ok]) / FLn[ok]
        print(f'[{nm}] partition f_ML+f_BL vs F_L (n>4e12, {ok.sum()} cols): '
              f'mean resid {resid.mean()*100:+.1f}%, rms {resid.std()*100:.1f}% '
              f'| f_ML {np.nanmin(fML[ok]):.0f}-{np.nanmax(fML[ok]):.0f}T, f_BL {np.nanmin(fBL[ok]):.0f}-{np.nanmax(fBL[ok]):.0f}T')
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig('hera_scratch/fan_analyze.png', dpi=95)
print('saved hera_scratch/fan_analyze.png')
print('READ: two branches tracking with n, summing to F_L(n) across density = ABA')
print('(partition robust, model-independent). A single branch on F_L would be ABC.')

Operational log (RECIPE FIX / TOOLING / PROTOCOL / FEEDBACK). Not a science notebook —

  exactly (TG [-6,+7], BG [-4.5,+4.5], Si [-50,+50]) and B cap 8.0 T on magnet.mag.vals

execute = read-only kernel-binding probe (measure cell 28). Re-entry after any E0
drop requires a fresh explicit grant.

TMO on `KRDG? A` (`heater.sample_temperature`). Root cause = the rig-card "LS335 has
two masters" quirk: per-point polling of the Lakeshore contends with the Grafana
logger and times out. Fix: do **not** `s.fp(heater.sample_temperature)` (or any
LS335 read) inside the per-point loop — record T once in `meas_config` (snapshot)
and lean on the Grafana log (timestamped) for any post-hoc T(t)/T(B) correction.
Applies to gate map + fans too. Run id 0 = the dud (metadata only, 0 rows).
gate-current-sanity-check.md fps `temperature` per point — fine on toploader, a trap
on VTI; the recipe should carry a VTI caveat. Corrected liveness re-run as a new cell.

## Gate C PASS (run 1) + gate map launched (run 2)

- Gate C liveness (measure cell 32, run 1): device alive — drain I flat 5.0 nA
  (current-bias OK), Rxx modulates (peak ~1.4k @ V_TG~0 at BG=0), sr1/sr2 corr 0.99
  but not identical (no grounded short), leakage floor (BG 35 pA, Si 0.57 nA on 1uA
  range). Promoted to ana cell 11. **Device R is LOW (~kohm)** -> my 5 mV sens

  fan-vti.md says fast axis `[k_tg.volt,k_bg.volt]` (generic) — for QC0426 substitute

Both Rxx channels show a TWO-tone pair, detrender-robust (identical across poly 3/5/7,
hann/blackman):
- sr1 (T3-T4): f_low 16.1 T + f_high 70.8 T (sum 87 T)
- sr2 (B4-B5): f_low 18.7 T + f_high 69.3 T (sum 88 T)
Sum ~ F_L: gate F_L=82.7 T, **Hall F_L=86.8 T** (n_Hall=8.4e12 from Rxy slope). Sum
17+70=87 ~ F_L(Hall) -> Luttinger partition holds -> TWO Fermi surfaces (ML+BL) ->
**ABA** on the electron side, both regions. ABC would be a single tone AT F_L.
- f_high ~70 T = f_BL (big bilayer pocket); f_low ~17 T = f_ML (small monolayer pocket).
